title: One-off probe tally (personal)
content:
Purpose: quick one-off probe to compare subtle latency/cost impact of 8-bit vs 4-bit quant on s-subset workload. Not a full sweep — just to capture weird outliers and rough numbers for 1:1 convos.

Run metadata:
- experiment_id: q1-probe-2025-02-12
- runner: q-p (local laptop -> dev-gpu pool)
- input_profile: 60% short (<=64 toks), 30% med (65-256), 10% long (257-1024)
- tokens/sample (avg): ~220

Quick table (each row = aggregated over 500 requests, median/90th/throughput/cost):
mode, model, quant, batch, median_lat_ms, p90_lat_ms, tok_per_sec, est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, notes
baseline, gptx-small, fp16, 1, 48, 120, 2200, 0.0075, stable
probe-A, gptx-small, int8, 1, 51, 135, 2100, 0.0061, slight var on long tails
probe-B, gptx-small, int4, 1, 68, 210, 2000, 0.0048, occasional GLITCH spike (~3% requests)
probe-C, gptx-small, int4, 4, 95, 350, 5400, 0.0042, batching helps throughput but p90 jumps for short inputs
probe-D, gptx-small, int8, 8, 160, 420, 17000, 0.0056, cost wins at scale, tail latency worse on mempressure

Observations (raw thoughts):
- int4 gives clear cost advantage (~35% lower est cost/1k) but median latency up ~40% for single-shot. Not surprising.
- Weird spike: int4 single (probe-B) shows ~3% requests with 2-3x latency. Likely GC/kv-cache reorg or cross-tenant eviction -> need logs. Add debug traces next run.
- Batching (probe-C) is good for throughput but short-request p90 suffers; our autoscaler/route should maybe keep small-latency path with max_batch=1 for interactive flows.
- int8 8-batch (probe-D) shows mem pressure causing p90 tail; consider smaller batch or fallback to int4-lower-batch for peak.

Quick checklist / next steps:
- [ ] Re-run probe-B with debug=true and capture kernel timeline + L2 mem stats (ticket MLINF-3220)
- [ ] Test same profiles on dedicated pool (reserved) to see if noisy neighbor goes away (Maya to help)
- [ ] Try hybrid: int4 for sequence<256 else int8 for long -> simulate routing policy (cheap heuristic)
- [ ] Add tiny eval on output quality for int4 on 100 random samples (sanity)

Notes-to-self (short):
- If garbage spikes persist, instrument KV cache hits by prefix length.
- Also check kernel selection logs: some runs used fallback matmul path (slow).
- Remember to tag any noticeable regressions to rollout PR (link above).

Scratch calculations: (approx)
- cost per tok baseline = $0.0075 / 2200 = 3.4e-6 $/tok -> ~ $3.4 per million tokens
- int4 cost per tok = $0.0048 / 2000 = 2.4e-6 $/tok -> ~ $2.4 per million tokens
-> ~30% saving if quality OK.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the 3% spike correlated with particular input prefixes? quick grep shows some correlation with longer initial prompt context (>512). Need more granular traces.
- Does our allocator trigger compaction on int4 more aggressively? compare allocator logs.

Slack crumbs / references:
- chat: #bench-room thread: "q1 probe int4 odd spike" (search)
- convo with Ravi: mentioned trying 'max_kv_cache=8' param to reduce compactions.

Bottom line (for now): int4 looks promising cost-wise but has instability on tails; not ready for full auto-rollout. Follow the debug run + dedicated pool test before proposing routing rule.

-- qp
